data.title: bn-3h64: emit and consume REGISTRY_DELTA in SealPack
data.description:
SealPack reserved section kind 10 and never emitted it, so pack-sealed stores kept the O(#names) registry pread path at open while loose stores took bn-26pp's .reg win.

EMIT: seal_consolidated stages the segment's $registry batches as a REGISTRY_DELTA section from the SAME encode_registry_delta call the loose path uses — the body IS a .reg image byte for byte (one encoder, one parser, one corruption-test surface). Staged after STREAM_FILTER and before EVENT_TYPE_IDS/PAYLOAD_COLUMNS so it stays in the front-of-file region open already touches. Directory crc32c + content_hash_prefix like every section, so bn-11g identity covers it (mess verify confirms: 32/32 packs 'trailer hash and every section checksum' + footer identity matched).

CONSUME: SealedSegmentIndex locates the section at open (one 48-byte SectionRef + a clone of the handle the pack's file-backed sections already hold) and read_registry_delta() preads it on demand, verifies the committed checksums, parses, and runs accepts_registry_delta against the pack's OWN STREAM_DIRECTORY + POINTER_BLOCKS — the cross-check adapts by the pack playing both roles .reg split between a sidecar and its sibling. Engine recovery asks the index first, falls through to .reg, then to preads. Fallback per segment, unchanged.

THE RULE (documented at the .reg emission site): a pack-sealed segment gets a section and NO sibling .reg. seal returns into seal_consolidated before that write; sealed_candidate files .reg under PIDX_SIBLING_EXTENSIONS only (a .seal's quarantine family is the pack alone) and the CLI layout map agrees.

MEASUREMENT (8 GiB / 250k streams, ABBA, fadvise DONTNEED, 6 rounds/cell, one binary): pack+section 265.7 ms vs loose+.reg 265.5 ms (+0.1%, null-control floor 2.8-4.0%) — target met. Section vs no-section 44.8x; .reg vs no-.reg 37.1x. Pre-bone the pack path was 44.9x slower than loose at that shape.

Full evidence in the bn-3h64 bone comment.
